name: Create new task issues
description:
- Bug: creating a new task lost the selected **project** and **cost budget** on the created chat.
- Traced to `SprintBoardView.onTaskCreated()`, which split the payload and only forwarded a hard-coded subset to chat creation.
- Fix 1: `estimation_cost` was being swallowed into `task` and discarded by `newSprintTask` — extracted and persisted via `updateChatInfo`.
- Fix 2: normalized `ProjectDetailt`'s emit shape (`project_id`/`id`/string) in `SprintBoardModals.onProjectSelected()`.
- Project still failing → suspected `project_id` must be passed **into** `newSprintTask(task)`, and `updateChatInfo`'s `{ chat, updates }` signature is unverified; awaiting `kanban.js`, `chats.js`, and `ProjectDetailt.vue`.

messages.content:
Create new task fails on:
 - Project selection is not preserved
 - Cost is not preserved

So new tasks don't have the selected project, nor the cost assigned.
Revoew all options to make sure all user preferences are past to the chat creation

## Root cause

`SprintBoardModals.vue` correctly emits **every** preference in the `task-created` payload — the bug is on the receiving side, in `SprintBoardView.onTaskCreated()`.

That handler splits the payload and only forwards a hard-coded subset to the metadata endpoint:

```js
const { project_id, users, deadline, ...task } = payload   // estimation_cost falls into `task`
const chat = await this.$storex.kanban.newSprintTask(task) // …and is silently ignored
```

Per the handler's own comment, `newSprintTask` **only understands the core fields** (`name`, `mode`, `status`, `parentId`, `profiles`, `llm_model`). So `estimation_cost` is handed to a function that discards it, and — because it is never re-added to `updates` — the budget is lost forever.

`project_id` *is* routed through `updateChatInfo`, so the second symptom points upstream at how the selection is captured in the modal.

### Preference audit (form → chat creation)

| Preference | Modal field | Emitted as | Routed via | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name | `newTask.name` | `name` | `newSprintTask` | ✅ |
| Mode / type | `newTask.mode` | `mode` | `newSprintTask` | ✅ |
| Status (column) | `newTask.status` | `status` | `newSprintTask` | ✅ |
| Parent | `newTask.parentId` | `parentId` | `newSprintTask` | ✅ |
| Profiles | `newTask.selectedProfiles` | `profiles` | `newSprintTask` | ✅ |
| LLM model | `newTask.llm_model` | `llm_model` | `newSprintTask` | ✅ |
| Project | `newTask.project_id` | `project_id` | `updateChatInfo` | ⚠️ capture |
| Assignees | `newTask.users` | `users` | `updateChatInfo` | ✅ |
| Deadline | `newTask.deadline` | `deadline` | `updateChatInfo` | ✅ |
| Cost budget | `newTask.estimation_cost` | `estimation_cost` | ~~`newSprintTask`~~ | ❌ **dropped** |

---

## Fix 1 — cost budget is dropped (`SprintBoardView.vue`)

Pull `estimation_cost` out of the payload too, and persist it alongside the other non-core preferences.

```js src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue
    async onTaskCreated(payload) {
      // `newSprintTask` only understands the core task fields (name, mode,
      // status, parentId, profiles, llm_model). Every other preference the user
      // picked in the dialog — project, assignees, deadline and the cost budget —
      // is persisted afterwards through the shared metadata endpoint so none of
      // them are silently dropped.
      const { project_id, users, deadline, estimation_cost, ...task } = payload
      const chat = await this.$storex.kanban.newSprintTask(task)
      if (!chat) return

      const updates = {}
      if (project_id) updates.project_id = project_id
      if (users?.length) updates.users = users
      if (deadline) updates.deadline = deadline
      if (estimation_cost != null) updates.estimation_cost = estimation_cost

      if (Object.keys(updates).length) {
        await this.$storex.chats.updateChatInfo({ chat, updates })
      }

      this.$emit('open-task', chat)
    },
```

---

## Fix 2 — project selection capture (`SprintBoardModals.vue`)

`onProjectSelected` only reads `project.project_id`. `ProjectDetailt` (a generic selector) can emit either the project object or its raw id, so normalize both shapes — otherwise a perfectly valid selection resolves to `null` and never reaches chat creation.

```js src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue
    onProjectSelected(project) {
      // ProjectDetailt may emit the full project (with `project_id` or `id`) or
      // just the id — normalize both so the selection survives to chat creation.
      this.newTask.project_id = project?.project_id
        ?? project?.id
        ?? (typeof project === 'string' ? project : null)
    },
```

No change is needed in `confirmNewTask()` — it already emits `project_id` and a normalized `estimation_cost` (`null` when empty/≤0), which matches the `!= null` guard added above.

---

## Anti-patterns avoided

- ❌ Spreading the whole payload into `newSprintTask` hoping it ignores unknown fields — can trigger backend validation errors.
- ❌ Re-binding `:cost` on `ChatCostSelector` — `cost` is the *spent* value; the *budget* is `estimation-cost` / `cost-changed`, which is already wired correctly.

## Verification checklist

- [ ] Create a task, pick a **non-default project** → open it → project persisted.
- [ ] Create a task with a **cost budget** (e.g. `500`) → open it → `estimation_cost === 500`.
- [ ] Create with **no** budget / no project → both stay `null` (no empty-string writes).
- [ ] Create a **subtask** with a parent that has a project → project inherits and sticks.
- [ ] If project *still* doesn't stick, the remaining suspect is `$storex.chats.updateChatInfo({ chat, updates })` — confirm it (a) accepts `project_id` and (b) mutates the **same** chat reference the kanban column renders, not just the API response.

I'll provide the full file content for both files with the fixes applied. ```vue src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue ``` ```vue src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardModals.vue ``` ### Changes summary **`SprintBoardView.vue`** — `onTaskCreated()`: - Destructure `estimation_cost` out of the payload so it is no longer swallowed into `task` (which `newSprintTask` discards). - Persist it via `updates.estimation_cost` when present (`!= null` guard, so `0`/empty stays untouched). **`SprintBoardModals.vue`** — `onProjectSelected()`: - Normalize the emit shape (`project_id`, `id`, or raw string) so a valid project selection is never lost before chat creation.

## Diagnosis

My earlier fix routes `project_id` through a *separate* `updateChatInfo` call **after** `newSprintTask`. Two things go wrong there:

1. **`updateChatInfo` almost certainly does not take `{ chat, updates }`.** If its real signature is `{ chatId, ...fields }` (or `{ id, ...updates }`), then `project_id` is never written — the call resolves without persisting anything. That's why the cost fix (also added to that same `updates` object) may *also* still be failing.
2. **The project must be part of the *creation* call**, not a follow-up patch. Your hint says it plainly: *"the selected project must be the `project_id` of the new task"* → `project_id` should be handed to `newSprintTask` (which sets the new chat's `project_id`), not applied afterwards.

## Fix — pass `project_id` directly into `newSprintTask`

```js src/components/kanban/board/SprintBoardView.vue
    async onTaskCreated(payload) {
      // `project_id` is a first-class field of the new task: it must be part of
      // the creation call so the chat is created *inside* the selected project
      // (and the kanban column renders it there). Follow-up metadata — assignees,
      // deadline and the cost budget — is persisted afterwards.
      const { users, deadline, estimation_cost, ...task } = payload
      const chat = await this.$storex.kanban.newSprintTask(task)
      if (!chat) return

      const updates = {}
      if (users?.length) updates.users = users
      if (deadline) updates.deadline = deadline
      if (estimation_cost != null) updates.estimation_cost = estimation_cost

      if (Object.keys(updates).length) {
        await this.$storex.chats.updateChatInfo({ chat, updates })
      }

      this.$emit('open-task', chat)
    },
```

Here `task` still contains `project_id` because it is **no longer destructured out**, so it flows into `newSprintTask(task)` untouched.
